summary: Episode 051, `STF: Sexually Transmitted Feelings`, begins with a speculative DVDASA wedding for Bobby and Quiet C. The room invents a public proposal, bachelor party, celebrity ceremony, and even a diamond implanted in Bobby's wart. None is an accepted plan, and Quiet C's protected name, friends, sexuality, photos, and relationship wishes remain outside retrieval metadata. The cast then subjects a prospective producer to an on-air employment interview about his appearance, residence, sexuality, family, private friend, pornography, and sexual history. He says the disclosures make him want to disappear and remains unsure about future appearances, even after David says he has the job. Employment does not create blanket media consent. His surname, address clues, family, private friend, and intimate history are withheld; the cast's sandwich test, sexual-orientation guesses, childhood theories, and amateur diagnoses are not biography. The candidate's stated interests in Design Media Arts, art direction, Ministry, Sonic Youth, and television remain usable professional and cultural context. The episode's running `STF` phrase means `sexually transmitted feelings`, an emotional metaphor rather than medicine. David then acknowledges that his protected Mexico City partner does not want him discussing her. He nevertheless recounts becoming attached while physically ill, overworked, and using an improperly obtained painkiller to mask symptoms during a three-week museum-scale art build. He describes compulsively flying to Las Vegas immediately after returning, despite a prior gambling problem and a reported casino chest-pain episode. A protected woman had offered to keep him away from casinos. One abstinent visit does not establish recovery. At her home, she repeatedly says sexual escalation is `too soon`, keeps his hands away, and says no. David describes using the tip of a finger to penetrate her anyway as a `test`, then continuing when she again says no. The record labels this reported sequence nonconsensual. Prior years of texting, arousal, kissing, dry humping, mortality claims, later intercourse, repeated sex, or her subsequent message cannot retroactively authorize the initial penetration. The woman remains unidentifiable. Her private breakup message is summarized, not reproduced; the room's attempt to identify her from origin, diet, religion, ethnicity, appearance, and guessed names is rejected. Her message clearly says she fears eventual heartbreak and wants friendship before deeper attachment; it is not rewritten as a gendered `test`. The episode also revisits how David publicly diminished Zell's intimate generosity while she was present, reinforcing the need to protect her metadata. Graphic illness and sanitation stories remain first-person testimony, not medical advice. Public corrections include SXSW, Aimee Teegarden, Nicolas Cage, Isamu Noguchi's Cube, Maury Showbizawitz, Goo Goo Dolls, Michael Bolton, Raku, Monta Ramen, Fry's Electronics, and Friday Night Lights characters Chad Clarke, Santiago Herrera, Bobby Reyes, and Herc. All named dialogue remains withheld pending an independently validated multi-speaker attribution result.

connections.note: The cast's elaborate fantasy is not evidence that Quiet C wanted a proposal, public ceremony, or searchable relationship profile.
A verbal claim by a dealer does not establish ethical provenance.
A job trial and later offer occur alongside intimate coercion; employment cannot serve as blanket recording consent.
His explicit distress is direct evidence to withhold surname, address clues, family, friend, and sex history.
A lucky name guess does not make a private person a public figure.
One appearance and employment do not authorize future inclusion or voice enrollment.
The recurring phrase becomes this episode's title but remains emotional metaphor, not medicine.

connections.note: This direct request strengthens the protected-partner policy across Episodes 050–051.
David describes completing a large body of work in three weeks after four years without an art show.
Medication is described as enabling eighteen-hour workdays while hiding illness; it is not productivity advice.
David reports abstaining on this trip but also identifies gambling as a prior life-dominating addiction.
Public venues locate the historical account without identifying the private woman.
The room acknowledges David diminished an intimate act while Zell was present, reinforcing why the archive does not amplify it.
The stated boundary appears before each attempted escalation and must remain visible.
Risk of death, prior texting, and Lisa Ling's alleged warning do not override a partner's refusal.
David describes penetrating after no to see whether she resists further; consent cannot be tested by violating it.
Later participation and arousal do not authorize the earlier act.
The archive summarizes the decision and emotional meaning instead of reproducing a private text verbatim.
Religion, diet, origin, war exposure, ethnicity, body, and name guesses are suppressed as a combined identification vector.
Chad Clarke, Santiago Herrera, Bobby Reyes, Herc, and `Texas forever` provide high-confidence cultural repairs.
